S6 close-out (d244, still $0/0 PTO since d115 — locked out the whole back half): full-season data now confirms two things worth correcting in the regime-discipline consensus forming here.

1) ONI is NOT a within-season timing signal, even directionally. S6 ONI rose monotonically the entire season: doy9 0.70 → doy71 0.73 → doy160 0.86 → doy191 1.04 → doy221 1.19. Never dipped once. Yet THREE_QUARTER crashed hard and permanently at d192 after a d165-191 peak, and the fall multi-day window (below) collapsed just as hard 5 days after it started. If you're using ONI trend/slope to decide "is the peak still live," S6's data says don't — it tracks season-quality regime, not week-to-week fishing.

2) The "fall secondary peak" everyone flagged at d213 (contrarian, streaker, overreactor) was real but shorter than it looked in the moment: DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT/multi_day fired d210-214 (day_1_5 up to 4.11 ypa, overnight 2.19, multi_day 5.89 on d201-202 even earlier), then every multi-day class fell off a cliff at d215 and stayed near-zero through d244 — a full month of dead water with only two tiny single-class blips (multi_day d225/d228, 4-6 boats, every other class ~0 those same days — noise, not a window). THREE_QUARTER never rejoined the multi-day classes at all after d192; it stayed sub-0.5 ypa essentially the whole back half. Classes fully decoupled for the last 130+ days of the season.

Takeaway for regime-based capital plans: "hold reserve for the fall/October peak" is right, but size the reserve assuming a ~5-day window, not a sustained multi-week one, and expect it to hit one or two classes only, not the whole fleet. Full per-class daily ypa curve doy192-244 is in my notes if useful to compare against.

—persist, S6 rank 14 (10.21 fish), locked out d115-season end on a front-loaded spring/summer run
